newsitem.title: CHINA: China to cut illiteracy by educating girls.
newsitem.headline: China to cut illiteracy by educating girls.

text.p: China wants more public donations to help girls in rural areas go to school and slash illiteracy among women, who account for the vast majority of Chinese who cannot read and write, officials said on Monday.
China had 160 million illiterate or semi-illiterate people aged 15 or above at the end of 1996, said an official of the State Statistical Bureau.

Up to 70 percent of China's illiterates, who accounted for about 13 percent of the country's population of 1.2 billion, were women, an official of the All-China Women's Federation said in a telephone interview.
The key to cutting the number of women illiterates was the education of girls, but many Chinese farmers were unwilling to spend money on educating daughters, officials and state media said.
Among children deprived of education due to poverty, about 70 percent were girls, the federation official said.
"China's traditional bias for boys over girls has resulted in the high drop-out rate of girls," he said.
In rural areas, many parents kept their daughters working at home and paid only for a son's education, he said.
A nationwide project launched by women's organisations and funded mainly through donations had helped about 430,000 girls in backward areas to go to school since 1989, he said.
But more donations from the public were needed to expand the project, he said.
"Our project only supports girls to try to strike a balance in education between girls and boys," he said.
The project provides 300 yuan ($36) a year to each girl going to school.
"If China can resolve the education problems of girls and women, many other problems would be solved at a stroke," he said.
